items.claim: Anthropic's biology research lab published what it describes as the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle. The vault comes from a bacteriophage and is built from 96 copies of a single protein; human vaults use 78. Anthropic says Claude helped with database search, DNA construct design, isolation-method optimization and microscopy data processing. A preprint has been submitted to bioRxiv.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete case of an AI lab using its model across a wet-lab structural biology workflow. The reported speedups are self-reported: purification took about 90 minutes instead of three days, and a first structural model was ready 34 hours later. They are not yet peer-reviewed.

verification.method: Confirmed on Anthropic's own research page (snapshot) that the publication exists and states these details; scientific findings and speedups remain Anthropic-reported pending the preprint

items.excerpt: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells.

items.claim: GitHub Copilot can now be used in Xcode's built-in coding assistant, in public preview. Requirements are Xcode 27.3 beta and macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later. All Copilot plans are supported, and the separate Copilot for Xcode extension remains available.
items.why_it_matters: iOS and macOS developers can use Copilot inside Xcode's native assistant instead of relying only on a third-party extension.
items.try_this: In Xcode 27.3 beta, open Xcode > Settings > Intelligence to set up GitHub Copilot in the coding assistant.

verification.method: Confirmed on the GitHub Changelog page (snapshot); not tested in Xcode

items.excerpt: The integration is now in public preview, available starting with Xcode 27.3 beta.

items.claim: OpenAI is bringing GPT-Image-2.6 to Codex and the API. It says the 2.6 versions of its Flare and Sunburst image models generate images 50% faster than before in the API. Flare is positioned for quick first passes, and Sunburst for consistent detail across edits.
items.why_it_matters: Faster API image generation lowers latency for iterative design workflows. The 50% speed figure is a vendor claim.

verification.method: Stated in OpenAI's official video descriptions; openai.com announcement page not snapshotted and speed figure not independently measured

items.excerpt: In the API, the 2.6 versions of Flare and Sunburst generate images 50% faster than before.
